art_changes: A wide organic tonal transition was requested over approximately25–35px at210px scale, simultaneously reducing peripheral vegetation contrast, dark floor shadows and density toward the ground.
Plains pointy proof was revised a second time to soften the top and shoulder boundaries; that proof supplied the shared edge-treatment reference for the remaining five edits.
Dense readable central crowns and terrain forms remain. Mountain summit silhouettes remain crisp; low vegetation and footslopes fade into the grassy ground.
The surrounding ground is painted toward grass.png; pixel identity is not claimed. Measured outside-hex background means are included per asset.
export: 210x210 sRGB RGB PNG, opaque. Whole generated source resized as one image; no masked painting or local pixel editing. Regular hex masks are used only for map/contact previews.
validation: Six formats and source dimensions checked. Visual checks at210px and reduced map scale assess the tonal transition. Outside-dark-green count is a color heuristic, not exact foreground segmentation.

proof_chain.prompt: Edit the FIRST reference image, a 210x210 Civilization V strategic-view-inspired deciduous forest tile, using the SECOND reference image as the exact surrounding grass ground palette and subtle ground texture. The user says the forest currently reads as a hard-edged dark blob in the middle of the hex. Make a real wide graduated transition from the existing dense forest into the grass. Preserve the upright composition, tree crown sizes, crowded dense central forest, main crown silhouettes and warm readable highlights. Keep the inner approximately 60 percent of the forest's radius crisp and dense. Across the outer 25 to 35 pixels of the forest footprint at final 210px scale, gradually fade the VEGETATION'S COLOR DIFFERENCE, local CONTRAST, SHADOW DEPTH and UNDERSTORY DENSITY into the grass, so the vegetation becomes increasingly intermixed with the ground and finally indistinguishable from it. This should resemble an irregular soft painted pigment/opacity falloff composited into an OPAQUE grass image, not merely a ragged crisp shrub border. Eliminate the continuous dark floor stain beneath the stand. Break the outermost continuous line: some low growth reaches farther, some grass intrudes inward; outer shadows become shallower and approach the base ground tone. The gradient must start visibly well inside the existing silhouette, not just add a 3-pixel blurred edge. Blend forest floor and cast shadows at the same time as foliage, without a continuous oval wall. There must be no outline that a viewer can trace all the way around the forest. Keep the core dark greens and clean clear tree forms; do not wash out the entire forest or make pastel art. No white glow, no fog halo, no empty lawn moat and no shrinking the whole stand into a small central icon. The background extends across the complete square, while all significant tree crowns and shadows stay within the original pointy-top full regular hex footprint. No hex outline, no visible polygon, no labels, no borders, no interface, no alpha. The output is just one square finished game tile. This is an edge color/tonal transition edit, not a new forest design.

Targeted correction of the FIRST reference tile (a dense forest already partly blended into grass). SECOND reference is the exact desired base grass image. Keep the first tile's interior mature crowns, sizes, dense forest, upright composition and rich core contrast unchanged. Finish the transition around the TOP and UPPER LEFT / UPPER RIGHT shoulders: they still look like a sharply ending raised cap. Paint a broad gradual reduction of the foliage's contrast, darkness and color difference from grass through the upper outer 25-35px at final 210px scale, just as the lower edge already softens, but more decisive. The uppermost adult tree crowns must NOT form a sharp continuous boundary against grass. Fade their outer paint into grass in shallow irregular translucent-pigment-like washes; blend their upper shadows and small shrubs simultaneously, until there is no traceable edge anywhere around the stand. This is a true smooth tonal gradient to the grass around ALL sides, not a hard silhouette with a few extra tiny shrubs. Keep the central 120x120px forest legible and crisp, no global blur or haze. Also bring all outer ground and the very outer faded vegetation back toward the SECOND image's muted sage grass colors (approximately RGB157,176,99), which are less yellow and less saturated than the first image ground (roughly151,175,77). Use the second image ground color as the actual surrounding canvas, not just vague inspiration. No yellow-green ground shift, no colored stain or dark ring beneath the stand, no white halo, no bare lawn moat. Maintain the same full-size forest footprint, pointy regular hex-compatible fitting, and opaque full square background. No visible hex border, no labels, no interface, no separate icons. Return one complete square finished game tile, not a comparison.

assets.prompt: Edit the FIRST reference image only. It is a finished dense deciduous forest plains game tile. The SECOND reference is the desired wide edge-blending treatment demonstrated on plains; apply that treatment to the first image, not its terrain design. The TOP and UPPER SHOULDER edges of the stand must fade too: uppermost crowns must not form a continuous sharp cap. Preserve the first image's composition, upright trees, mature crown scale, dense closed-canopy core, and flat ground. The problem is a dark forest blob with an abrupt border. Make a true gradual fade of vegetation color difference, shadow depth, local contrast, and plant density into the grass over a wide 25 to 35 pixels at final 210px tile scale. The fade begins visibly INSIDE the existing outer forest silhouette and follows a soft irregular organic footprint. Outermost growth and the surrounding ground gradually mix into the shared muted sage grass hue (roughly RGB157,176,99), avoiding a new saturated yellow-green field; outermost growth gradually mixes into this base grass hue and brightness and then becomes indistinguishable from the ground. This is an opacity-like soft pigment falloff PAINTED INTO AN OPAQUE TILE, rather than a crisp fringe of shrubs. Fade the forest floor and cast shadows too; eliminate any continuous dark oval or hexagonal ground stain. Grass enters the woodland in irregular shallow bays; lighter sparse low understory reaches out between those bays. Avoid any single traceable continuous line of forest ending. Keep the interior forest crisp, rich green, dense, and dark enough for game readability. Preserve tree sizes; no oversized trees on plains or tiny trees in mountains.  No white fog, glow or halo; do not blur or pastel the whole image. No broad empty lawn moat, no shrinking the forest to a small central island, no adding detail or leaf speckling. preview_map.title: Все готовые типы местности · по 2d6
preview_map.dice_method: Each type independently rolled with two crypto.randomInt(1,7) draws, once. Both orientations reuse the same rolls and axial cell assignment.
preview_map.layout_method: Compact hex field partitioned into exact-size connected regions; complement connectivity preserved at each carving step. Layout attempts do not reroll dice.
